title: Rising above bias
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When did you last choose a mechanic, a doctor or an advisor without knowing their field?

Jose said: the common denominator of these people is that they are trying to rise above people's individual biases. He asked: does this guy have a bias? A student said: and he does that through challenging them. Jose said: that's exactly what he's doing.

Jose gave an example. When I go to the mechanic, he said, I am immediately on alert, because he will lift the hood and quickly realize I know nothing. How do I protect myself? He says: this is two thousand dollars. I'll ask questions to see if he is lying, and use a totally different knowledge base to judge whether I am choosing the right mechanic.
That is the essence of how these people can run multiple businesses, he said.

Jose said that educational systems package knowledge into little packages, engineering 101, 102, and give you five years of engineering. It becomes meaningful and easy to remember and creates a structure for you. What happens to that?

A student said: the teacher ends up passing on any limiting beliefs around those packages to the students. Another clarified later: it isn't the packaging that causes it. Any teacher will pass on their framework of thinking.

Jose said he can go on tangents and throw things on a wall and the students have to synthesize. Schools want you to leave with a knowledge base, so they organize it in chunks. Some schools go the opposite way and leave it open.
Where did a teacher's framework become yours without you noticing?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one field where you know nothing and depend on someone else.
Write three questions you would ask to test them.
Write what you have taken from a teacher as a limit.
Write how you could test whether it is true.
Write whose bias you most need to rise above.

check.q: What did Jose say these leaders try to rise above?
How did Jose protect himself with a mechanic?
choices: He asked questions and used another knowledge base

check.q: What did a student say teachers pass on?
choices: Their framework of thinking, including limiting beliefs

recap: Rise above bias by testing it. Notice the limits a teacher handed you.
